notes.title: Etheldia Pepper v2.2
notes.content:
Fixed an exploit via mouse which enabled infinite attacks per turn. Shoutout to Wehboy for discovering this.

Also fixed a few typos in the dialogue I noticed while replaying the game.

notes.title: Etheldia Pepper Version 2.0
notes.content:
Etheldia Pepper has updated to version 2.0. Take the knight challenge and defeat 50 enemies in a row to obtain the legendary blade, Excalibur!

Following completion of the story campaign, Colthan can now gain access to the chief hut in the centre of town, and enter the knight challenge. Test the strength of Colthan and his team by defeating as many knights in a row as you can. This update also features minor bugfixes, typo fixes, and a couple of new music tracks and SFX. 

With this update I'm continue to conclude working on this game in order to begin work on the next title in the series. I will however fix any game breaking bugs that appear. I hope you enjoy the update, and look forward to more Etheldia content in future!

notes.title: Nuzlocke Mode: V1.2
notes.content:
Looking for a challenging new way to experience the world of Etheldia? Nuzlocke mode lets you replay the game with a unique set of rules to change how you think about the game. A popular fan challenge in the Pokemon community, the Etheldia Nuzlocke mode works similarly and changes the game in the following ways:

1. You can only recruit the first character you encounter on each new route. (Recruit rates are 100%)
2. Characters are given automatically generated names to foster attachment. (Names are changeable)
3. If the HP of a character falls to zero at any time that character cannot be used again.
4. If the HP of Colthan falls to zero the challenge is over. (Game file can still be played as normal)

These rules up the stakes of each encounter and make you really think about your strategy for approaching the game. As a reward for successfully completing the challenge, Colthan will be gifted a special weapon at the end of the game. Also included in this update is a fix to the way speed and characters turns are calculated, and a few other minor bug fixes.

Moving forward I'm planning probably one more major update to Etheldia Pepper, featuring more postgame content in the form of the Knights Tournament. All of the graphics for this have already been completed and the programming phase can begin. If you have any suggestions for extra content or things you'd like to see improved please get in touch and I'll see if I can add it in for the next version!

-Hippo

notes.title: Etheldia Pepper Release!
notes.content:
Update 16/4/20
I've updated the game to version 1.1, mainly minor bugfixes and fixing a couple of typos.

------

Thanks everyone for your patience, the game is now live and released into the wild!

Please let me know about any bugs, particularly anything game breaking, as well as any typos in dialogue as there's bound to be a few of those. I will try to get any issues fixed as soon as possible.

Looking to the future, I'm planning a free update in the coming months with some additional post game content and probably a nuzlocke mode as a challenge. If there's any quality of life improvements you think could be made to the game let me know and I will try to include some in this update also. After this I will move on to beginning work on the next title in the Etheldia series.

I hope you enjoy the game! 
-Hippo

notes.title: A Sign of the Times
notes.content:
So, today is the release date for Etheldia Pepper. The game is finished, and it's all uploaded Steam, but I'm unable to release it. For those who don't know, before you can publish a game on Steam the build has to be approved by its release team. For context, Steam suggests that this process takes 2-3 days usually, but to allow for 5. I submitted the Etheldia Pepper build for approval on the 25th of March, and the game has yet to be approved, 20 days later. Apparently due to the pandemic, the Steam review team are currently working from home so there are delays in the approval process.

It's the first time I've heard of a developer waiting for a platform to release their game and not the other way around so it's a bit of a weird feeling but I've tried reaching out to Steam and the message I got back is that there's not much I can do other than be patient and wait. It feels really good to have finished the game though. I wasn't confident when I set out that I would be able to make the kind of game I envisioned in the time I had allocated but I'm proud to say that I think it's turned out to be a better and much more polished game than I believed possible at the beginning.

I apologize for the delay, and will post an updated release as soon as I learn more. In the meantime, if you have any questions about the game or in general, I'll be happy to answer them.

Thanks,
Hippo.
